skill.name: code-review
skill.description: Review code changes from a chosen fixed point against repository standards and the originating specification, using separate standards and spec review passes.
skill.summary: Review a branch or work-in-progress diff against coding standards and product requirements.
skill.author: mattpocock

content.user_title: Review Code Against Standards and Specs
content.value_statement: Code reviews can miss whether changes follow project rules and match the requested work. This skill separates standards review from specification review so each concern is visible.
actual_capabilities: Compares HEAD with a user supplied fixed point using a three-dot git diff.
Checks changed code against documented repository standards and a built-in code-smell baseline.
Checks implementation changes against an originating issue, PRD, or specification when available.
Runs standards and spec review as separate sub-agent passes to keep findings independent.
Reports Standards and Spec findings in separate sections with counts and worst issue per axis.
limitations: Requires a valid fixed point such as a branch, tag, or commit SHA.
Spec review is skipped or limited when no issue, PRD, or specification is available.
Findings depend on accessible repository standards and issue-tracker context.
It reviews diffs and documentation; it does not replace tests or runtime verification.

use_cases.title: Review a feature branch before opening a pull request
use_cases.description: Compare the branch against main and identify standards issues or missing specification requirements.

use_cases.title: Check implementation against a product requirement
use_cases.description: Use an issue, PRD, or spec file to confirm the diff matches the requested behavior.

use_cases.title: Separate style concerns from scope concerns
use_cases.description: Keep coding-standard feedback separate from spec-compliance feedback during review.

prompt_templates.title: Basic branch review
prompt_templates.scenario: You want a simple review against the main branch.

prompt_templates.title: Review since a specific commit
prompt_templates.scenario: You know the exact starting commit for the work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the changes since commit abc123 against our standards and the spec.

prompt_templates.title: Review with a spec file
prompt_templates.scenario: You have a local PRD or specification document.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review since main using docs/specs/checkout-flow.md as the spec source.

prompt_templates.title: Review a work-in-progress branch
prompt_templates.scenario: You want independent standards and scope feedback before finishing the work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review since origin/main. Keep Standards and Spec findings separate, and note if any spec requirement is missing.

output_examples.input: Review since main for a branch that changes payment form validation.
output: Standards: one duplicated validation branch found in the changed form file.
Spec: the new card-error copy is implemented, but the required retry behavior is missing.
Summary: Standards has one judgement call. Spec has one missing requirement.

output_examples.input: Review since HEAD~3 with no available spec.
output: Spec: skipped because no issue, PRD, or spec was available.
Summary: Standards has zero findings. Spec was not evaluated.

best_practices: Provide a clear fixed point, such as main, origin/main, or a commit SHA.
Point to the issue, PRD, or spec file when the branch name does not reveal it.
Run normal tests and type checks separately after using this review.
anti_patterns: Do not use it without a fixed point unless you are ready to clarify the comparison target.
Do not treat code-smell findings as hard failures without human judgement.
Do not use the spec review as a substitute for product acceptance testing.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews a git diff against repository coding standards and the originating specification or issue.

faq.question: Why are Standards and Spec reported separately?
faq.answer: A change can follow project style while implementing the wrong behavior, or match the spec while violating standards.

faq.question: Does it require a specification?
faq.answer: No. If no specification exists, the Spec section is skipped and the Standards review can still run.

faq.question: Can it review work in progress?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review any non-empty diff between HEAD and a valid fixed point.

faq.question: Does it run tests?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on review findings from the diff, standards, and spec context.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
